## File: README.md

# @mgpl-diagnostics/report-reader

Reads report PDFs from our partner labs (**Hy Patho Lab** and **Clinova Pathlabs**) and turns them into
typed JSON:

- every result: the value as printed, unit, reference range (multi-line ranges kept), method, and an H/L flag;
- patient, sample and booking details, plus registered, collected, received and reported dates;
- the signatories: name, qualification, registration number, role, and the **signature image** with its fingerprint;
- **NABL accreditation evidence** per page, so each test knows whether the performing lab marked it accredited.

From this our own report design can say, for every test, **who performed it** (Clinova or Hy Patho),
**who reported it** (which pathologist), and whether it was **done in a NABL-accredited lab**.

```ts
import { extractReport, labelFor } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/report-reader";

const { report, images } = await extractReport(pdfBytes, { signatures: knownSignaturesFromDb });
for (const test of report.tests) {
  console.log(test.name, test.parameters.length, labelFor(report, test).text);
  // "LIPID PROFILE 7 Performed at Clinova Pathlabs (NABL accredited, MC-…) · Reported by Dr …, MD (…)"
}
```

## No OCR needed, so values are exact

These PDFs come out of the labs' software with a real text layer. The reader takes each character from
the PDF itself, at its position, so values are never misread as they can be with OCR (`0` vs `O`,
`1` vs `l`, a dropped decimal point). The work is in the layout: matching each value to the right row
and column. Signatures are images; they are identified by fingerprint, not read.

A scanned paper report (a photo, with no text layer) is **not** supported and is rejected as unsupported.

### Measured accuracy

Run on 165 real reports (136 Hy Patho Lab, 29 Clinova; 576 pages). The reports stay on the lab's own
machine; the numbers come from `npm run validate` and `npm run recall`:

| Check | Hy Patho | Clinova |
| --- | --- | --- |
| reports read without error | 136 / 136 | 29 / 29 |
| numeric results printed in the result column and extracted with the same value and row name | 3,389 / 3,389 | 499 / 499 |
| reports with patient name, age, sex and all dates | 136 / 136 | 29 / 29 |
| reports with a named medical signatory | 136 / 136 ¹ | 29 / 29 |
| time per report (average) | ~0.17 s | ~0.25 s |

¹ Hy Patho prints the doctor's name only inside the signature image, so each new signature has to be
named once in the signature registry (see below). Until then it comes back as `name: null` with its
image and a warning.

The recall check finds result values directly from text positions, without the parser's row logic, and
confirms each one appears among the extracted results. Units, ranges, methods and test grouping were
reviewed by hand on a sample. If a lab changes its report template, run both scripts again.

## Install

GitHub Packages, scope `@mgpl-diagnostics`:

```bash
npm install @mgpl-diagnostics/report-reader
```

Node 20 or newer. The only runtime dependency is `pdfjs-dist`.

## API

### `extractReport(pdf: Uint8Array, options?) → { report, images }`

| option | |
| --- | --- |
| `file` | file name, kept in `report.source.file` |
| `signatures` | `KnownSignature[]`: signatures you have named before (see below) |
| `signatureImages` | keep signature pixels in `images` (default `true`) |

Throws `UnsupportedReportError` for any PDF that is not from a supported lab.

`images` maps a signatory id to `{ width, height, rgba }`; `toPng(image)` turns it into PNG bytes.

### `report` (`ExtractedReport`)

```
source        { file?, sha256, lab: "hypatho" | "clinova", labName, processedAt?, pages }
patient       { name?, title?, ageText?, ageYears?, sex?, patientId? }
sample        { bookingId?, barcodes[], sampleIds[], labCode?, collectedAt?, referredBy?, customer?, ordered[] }
dates         { registered?, collected?, received?, reported? }   ISO local time (IST) "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm"
tests[]       { name, department?, sampleType?, sampleId?, reported?, method?, mark?,
                parameters[]: { name, value, unit?, range?, method?, flag: "H" | "L" | "", group? },
                notes?, pages[], signedBy[] (signatory ids), accredited? }
signatories[] { id, name | null, qualification?, registration?, title?, role, medical,
                signature { sha, dhash, width, height }, source: "text" | "registry" | "unknown", pages[] }
accreditation[] { body: "NABL", certificate?, evidence: ("logo" | "text")[], pages[] }
warnings[]    things a person should look at (an unnamed signature, a test without results…)
```

- `value` is exactly as printed (`"7.3"`, `">2000.00"`, `"Negative"`). `flag` is the lab's printed flag,
  or else computed from a numeric value and a simple range (`a - b`, `< x`, `<= x`, `> x`, `Up to x`).
  Interpretive ranges such as "<200 Desirable" get no computed flag.
- `accredited`: `true` when every page of the test carries the performing lab's NABL mark or legend;
  `false` when the report uses NABL marks but not on this test's pages; absent when the report has no
  NABL marks at all (Hy Patho reports carry none).
- `role` is one of `pathologist | biochemist | microbiologist | consultant | manager | unknown`, and
  `medical` is true for doctors (`Dr …`, MD, DNB…). Only medical signatories count as "reported by".

### `labelFor(report, test) → ProvenanceLabel`

The line to print beside a test on our own report, plus its parts:
`{ performedBy, performedAt?, reportedBy[], accreditation?, sourceSha256, text }`.

### Signature registry (`KnownSignature`)

```ts
{ name, qualification?, registration?, title?, role?, lab?, sha?: string[], dhash?: string[] }
```

Matched by exact pixel hash first, then by perceptual hash (a few bits apart), so re-encoded copies
still match. **Keep the registry in your database, not in source control.** This package ships no
names or signatures of real people.

Clinova prints names and titles under each signature, so Clinova signatories are named from the text.
If a registered signature appears beside a different printed name, a warning is added.

## Rules for using the output

1. **Accreditation belongs to the performing lab, and only to tests it marks.** Say "performed at a NABL
   accredited laboratory (Certificate No. …)" next to those tests only. Never present it as our own
   accreditation, and never print the NABL logo on our reports. NABL does not allow its mark to be
   used by a lab it has not accredited.
2. **A signature belongs to its source PDF.** Show a partner doctor's signature only next to results
   extracted from the same PDF (`source.sha256`), never on other reports.
3. **Patient data.** Extracted reports and signature images are patient and personal data. Store them
   privately, never in a repository, never in logs.

## CLI

```bash
npx report-reader report.pdf [more.pdf …] [--out private/extracted] [--signatures known.json]
```

Writes `<name>.json` and `signatures/<id>.png`. The default output folder is git-ignored.

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run typecheck
npm test            # generates fictional fixtures (scripts/make-fixtures.ts), then runs test/
npm run build
npm run validate -- <folder-of-real-pdfs> [--signatures known.json]   # aggregate stats only
npm run recall -- <folder-of-real-pdfs>                               # value-level cross-check
npm run llms        # refresh llms-full.txt
```

Real reports never enter this repository. Tests use fictional reports drawn in the same layouts.
Layout notes for each lab are in [docs/formats.md](docs/formats.md), and the backend plan is in
[docs/backend-integration.md](docs/backend-integration.md).

## File: AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md — @mgpl-diagnostics/report-reader

Reads partner-lab report PDFs (Hy Patho Lab, Clinova Pathlabs) into typed JSON: results, patient and
sample details, dates, signatories with signature images, and NABL evidence per test. Used by the `api`
to import partner results. The backend plan is in [docs/backend-integration.md](docs/backend-integration.md),
and the layout of each lab in [docs/formats.md](docs/formats.md).

## Map

```
src/index.ts          extractReport, detectLab, UnsupportedReportError; resolves signatories + NABL per test
src/pdf.ts            pdfjs text layer → lines with x/y; images with placement, pixels, sha + dHash; toPng
src/table.ts          column split from the table header row, H/L flags, METHOD_LINE
src/text.ts           dates (→ ISO IST), ages, titles, signatory text, header key/value columns
src/registry.ts       accreditation marks (NABL/ilac artwork), signature lookup (caller's registry)
src/label.ts          labelFor(report, test): "Performed at … · Reported by …" (+ NABL only when marked)
src/labs/hypatho.ts   Hy Patho parser
src/labs/clinova.ts   Clinova parser
src/cli.ts            report-reader <pdf…> → JSON + signature PNGs (default out: private/, git-ignored)
src/types.ts          output model
scripts/make-fixtures.ts  fictional reports in both layouts (test/fixtures/, git-ignored)
scripts/validate.ts   aggregate stats over real reports (local only, prints no patient data)
scripts/recall.ts     value-level cross-check over real reports (local only)
test/extract.test.ts  node:test on the fictional fixtures
```

## Rules

1. **Never commit real reports, extracted JSON, signature images, or anything derived from them.**
   `private/`, `*.pdf` and `test/fixtures/` are git-ignored. Fixtures are fictional and drawn by
   `scripts/make-fixtures.ts`. Validation output must stay aggregate (counts, not names or values).
2. **No real people in source.** Partner doctors' names, registration numbers and signature hashes are
   data the caller passes in (`ExtractOptions.signatures`), kept in the api database. Accreditation
   artwork hashes (`ACCREDITATION_MARKS`) are fine: they are logos, not people.
3. **NABL belongs to the performing lab, per test.** `accredited` is true only when the test's pages
   carry the partner's mark. Never word anything as MGPL's own accreditation. Never suggest printing
   the NABL logo on our reports.
4. **A signature belongs to its source PDF** (`source.sha256`). APIs here must never hand out a
   signature apart from the report it came from.
5. **Values are as printed.** Do not normalise or convert result values or units. Flags are the
   printed ones, else computed only from simple numeric ranges.
6. **Parser changes need real-report checks.** Before merging a change to `src/labs/*` or `src/table.ts`,
   the owner runs `npm run validate` and `npm run recall` on the local real reports. Recall must stay
   at 100%, and the README numbers must be updated if they change. CI runs only the fictional tests.
7. **No OCR.** Supported PDFs have a text layer. A PDF without one is rejected (`UnsupportedReportError`)
   rather than guessed at.
8. Node ≥ 20, ESM, strict TypeScript. The only runtime dependency is `pdfjs-dist`, pinned exactly
   (its legacy build is what runs in Node).

## Commands

```bash
npm install
npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build
npm run validate -- <folder> [--signatures known.json]
npm run recall -- <folder>
npm run llms          # regenerate llms-full.txt (CI checks it)
```

## Repository rules

`main` takes pull requests only: squash merge, 1 code-owner review (`@BackStacked`), the `ci` check
required. Rules come from `mgpl-diagnostics/.github` (`scripts/protect-repos.mjs`). Releases: bump
`package.json`, tag `vX.Y.Z`, and the publish workflow pushes to GitHub Packages.

## Licence

All rights reserved (see LICENSE).

## File: docs/backend-integration.md

# Backend integration: importing partner-lab reports

This is the brief for wiring `@mgpl-diagnostics/report-reader` into the `api` repo (GraphQL Yoga on
Fastify), db-kit, auth-kit and report-kit. Read `api/AGENTS.md` and `api/docs/13-adding-a-feature.md`
first. This file covers only what is specific to imported reports.

## Why

MGPL collects samples and sends some of them to partner labs (Hy Patho Lab, Raipur; Clinova Pathlabs,
Secunderabad). Each partner returns a PDF report. Today the results are typed in again by hand. With
this feature, staff upload the partner's PDF, the results fill in automatically, and our report shows
for each test:

- **performed at**: the partner lab, and its city when the report prints it;
- **reported by**: the partner's doctor (name, qualification, registration), with their signature
  taken from that same PDF;
- **NABL**: "Performed at a NABL accredited laboratory (Certificate No. MC-3860)", only on the tests
  the partner marked as accredited.

## What the package gives you

```ts
import { extractReport, labelFor, toPng, UnsupportedReportError, type KnownSignature } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/report-reader";

const { report, images } = await extractReport(pdfBytes, { file: fileName, signatures: knownSignatures });
// report: ExtractedReport (README → "report"); images: Map<signatoryId, { width, height, rgba }>
// labelFor(report, test) → { performedBy, performedAt?, reportedBy[], accreditation?, sourceSha256, text }
```

- Deterministic and fast: about 0.2 s per report, no network, no OCR, no model files.
- Node only (it uses `node:crypto` and `node:zlib`). Add it to `api` like the other kits:
  `"@mgpl-diagnostics/report-reader": "^0.1.0"`, then commit the lockfile.
- Measured on 165 real reports: every printed numeric result was extracted with the right value
  under the right row. See README → "Measured accuracy".

## Non-negotiable rules

1. **NABL belongs to the performing lab, per test.** Show the NABL line only when
   `test.accredited === true`, worded as the partner's accreditation ("performed at a NABL accredited
   laboratory, Certificate No. …"). MGPL is not accredited by this. **Never draw the NABL or ilac
   logo** on our reports: only the lab NABL accredited may use the mark. Hy Patho reports carry no
   marks, so their tests get no NABL line.
2. **A signature only appears with results from its own PDF.** Store each signatory with the
   `sourceSha256` of the PDF it came from. Render a partner signature only on a report whose results
   came from that same PDF. Never let a stored partner signature be picked for another report, and
   never use one as MGPL's own signatory.
3. **"Reported by" means medical signatories only** (`signatory.medical === true`). Lab managers'
   signatures are on the PDF too, but they are not clinical sign-off.
4. **Our staff still verify.** Imported results enter the normal flow (`saveResults` → `verifyReport`),
   unchanged. Import never releases a report on its own.
5. **Patient data.** The original PDF, the extracted JSON and the signature PNGs are patient or
   personal data. Store them privately, tenant-scoped, and never in logs, fixtures or repositories.
   Tests use fictional PDFs; `report-reader`'s `scripts/make-fixtures.ts` shows how to draw one.
6. **Signature registry entries are data, not code.** Doctors' names and signature hashes live in the
   database, entered by an authorised user. Nothing about real partner doctors goes into source.

## Data model (db-kit, both PostgreSQL and MongoDB)

All three are tenant-scoped (`orgId`), audited, and support both adapters (rule 8 of `api/AGENTS.md`).

**`external_reports`**: one row per uploaded PDF.

| field | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id, orgId, branchId | | |
| bookingId | id, nullable | set when matched to a booking |
| lab | `"hypatho" \| "clinova"` | |
| labName, processedAt | string | |
| sourceSha256 | string | **unique per org**: uploading the same PDF twice returns the existing row |
| fileName | string | |
| pdf | bytes, or an object-storage key | original file; private |
| extracted | JSON | the full `ExtractedReport`, stored as is so it can be re-checked later |
| status | `"extracted" \| "matched" \| "applied" \| "rejected"` | |
| warnings | string[] | from the extractor and from booking matching |
| uploadedBy, uploadedAt, appliedBy?, appliedAt? | | |

**`external_signatories`**: the signature registry, one row per partner doctor or signer.

| field | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id, orgId | | |
| lab | LabId | |
| name, qualification, registration, title, role | | as `KnownSignature` |
| sha | string[] | pixel hashes seen for this person |
| dhash | string[] | perceptual hashes |
| createdBy, createdAt, verifiedBy? | | an authorised user names a signature once |

Load the org's rows as `KnownSignature[]` and pass them to `extractReport`. Cache them per org in
Redis through db-kit's cache layer, and clear the cache on write.

**`external_signatures`**: the signature images, one per (sourceSha256, signatory sha).

| field | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| orgId, externalReportId, sourceSha256 | | ties the image to its PDF (rule 2) |
| sha, dhash, width, height | | |
| png | bytes | from `toPng(images.get(id))`; private |

## Results provenance

Each `Report` (one per test, in our schema) created from an import also gets a provenance record.
Use a nullable JSON column on the report, or a separate `report_provenance` table:

```ts
interface ResultProvenance {
  externalReportId: string;
  sourceSha256: string;
  lab: "hypatho" | "clinova";
  performedBy: string;          // labelFor(...).performedBy
  performedAt?: string;
  reportedBy: { signatoryId: string; name: string | null; qualification?: string; registration?: string; title?: string; role: string }[];
  accreditation?: { body: "NABL"; certificate?: string; text: string };
  sourceTestName: string;       // the partner's own test name, for audit
  sourceSampleId?: string;
  sourceReportedAt?: string;    // ISO local (IST)
}
```

If staff edit a value after import, keep the provenance and audit the change. The report then shows
"performed at …" as before, and our verifier signs as usual.

## Permissions (auth-kit)

Add these to auth-kit's `PERMISSIONS`. Every permission the api uses must exist there.

- `reports.import`: upload a partner PDF, match it to a booking, and apply it.
- `signatories.manage`: name a partner signature, and edit or remove one.

Both are checked per branch (`authorize(ctx, perm, branchId)`), as everywhere else.

## GraphQL (module `lab` or a new `imports` module)

One endpoint, no REST routes (api rule 1). Files travel as base64, the same way `Document` does.
Cap the input at 15 MB (`limits.ts`).

```graphql
enum ExternalLab { hypatho clinova }
enum ExternalReportStatus { extracted matched applied rejected }

type ExternalReport {
  id: ID!
  lab: ExternalLab!
  labName: String!
  processedAt: String
  sourceSha256: String!
  fileName: String
  status: ExternalReportStatus!
  booking: Booking
  patient: ExternalPatient!          # name, title, ageText, ageYears, sex, patientId
  sample: JSON!                      # bookingId, barcodes, sampleIds, labCode, collectedAt, referredBy, customer, ordered
  dates: JSON!
  tests: [ExternalTest!]!
  signatories: [ExternalSignatory!]!
  accreditation: [ExternalAccreditation!]!
  warnings: [String!]!
  uploadedAt: DateTime!
}

type ExternalTest {
  index: Int!                        # position in extracted.tests
  name: String!
  department: String
  sampleType: String
  sampleId: String
  reported: String
  method: String
  mark: String
  accredited: Boolean
  parameters: [ExternalParameter!]!  # name value unit range method flag group
  notes: String
  signedBy: [ExternalSignatory!]!
  label: String!                     # labelFor(report, test).text
  suggestedTestCode: String          # catalog-kit search(name) top hit, for staff to confirm
}

type ExternalSignatory {
  id: ID!                            # signature sha
  name: String
  qualification: String
  registration: String
  title: String
  role: String!
  medical: Boolean!
  source: String!                    # text | registry | unknown
  signature: Document                # PNG as base64, only for users with reports.import, only for this PDF
}

type ExternalAccreditation { body: String!, certificate: String, evidence: [String!]!, pages: [Int!]! }

extend type Query {
  externalReport(id: ID!): ExternalReport!
  externalReports(bookingId: ID, status: ExternalReportStatus, first: Int = 50, after: String): ExternalReportConnection!
  externalSignatories(lab: ExternalLab): [ExternalSignatoryRecord!]!
}

extend type Mutation {
  # upload → extract → store; returns the existing row if this PDF was uploaded before (sourceSha256)
  importExternalReport(pdfBase64: String!, fileName: String, bookingId: ID): ExternalReport!
  # tie it to a booking when it was not given at upload or was wrong; checks patient name/age/sex and adds warnings on mismatch
  matchExternalReport(id: ID!, bookingId: ID!): ExternalReport!
  # write results into our Reports: one mapping per external test → our catalog test code
  applyExternalReport(id: ID!, mappings: [ExternalTestMapping!]!): [Report!]!
  rejectExternalReport(id: ID!, reason: String!): ExternalReport!
  # name a Hy Patho signature once; re-extracts the org's unnamed imports in the background
  nameExternalSignature(input: ExternalSignatoryInput!): ExternalSignatoryRecord!
}

input ExternalTestMapping { testIndex: Int!, testCode: String!, include: Boolean = true }
input ExternalSignatoryInput { sha: String!, lab: ExternalLab!, name: String!, qualification: String, registration: String, title: String, role: String }
```

Error codes (add, never rename): `UNSUPPORTED_REPORT` (from `UnsupportedReportError`),
`REPORT_ALREADY_APPLIED`, `BOOKING_PATIENT_MISMATCH` (a warning unless staff confirm),
`FILE_TOO_LARGE`.

## Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant S as Staff (client)
  participant A as api
  participant R as report-reader
  participant D as db-kit
  S->>A: importExternalReport(pdfBase64, bookingId?)
  A->>A: authorize reports.import; size cap; sha256
  A->>D: find external_reports by (orgId, sha256)
  alt new PDF
    A->>D: load external_signatories → KnownSignature[]
    A->>R: extractReport(bytes, { signatures })
    A->>D: store PDF, extracted JSON, signature PNGs (with sourceSha256)
  end
  A-->>S: ExternalReport (tests, labels, warnings, suggested test codes)
  S->>A: matchExternalReport / applyExternalReport(mappings)
  A->>D: createReport + saveResults per mapping, with ResultProvenance
  S->>A: verifyReport (unchanged flow)
```

- **Where extraction runs.** Run it inline for files up to about 5 MB. Larger files go to a job
  (`src/jobs/`, BullMQ or in-process, api rule 12): the payload carries the `externalReportId` and the
  actor, never the file or a token. CPU work stays off the request path for large files.
- **Booking match.** Compare the booking patient with `report.patient` (name case-insensitively and
  without titles, sex, age within ±1 year). Hy Patho's `sample.collectedAt` and Clinova's
  `sample.customer` name our collection centre, which is a useful check. A mismatch is a warning that
  staff must confirm. Never a silent apply.
- **Test mapping.** Suggest `catalog-kit` `search(test.name, { limit: 1 })` and let staff confirm.
  Map each `parameters[].name` to our catalog parameter by search within the chosen test. Keep
  unmatched parameters as entered (`ResultInput` takes a free `parameter` string).
- **Values.** Copy `value`, `unit`, `range`, `flag` as extracted (`ResultInput` matches). Do not
  recompute ranges from our catalog for imported results: the partner's range applies to the
  partner's method.
- **Unnamed signatures.** Hy Patho signatures come back with `name: null` until named.
  `nameExternalSignature` adds the sha and dhash to `external_signatories`. Then re-run extraction
  (from the stored PDF) on that org's imports in status `extracted` or `matched` that contain that sha.

## report-kit: printing provenance

report-kit currently prints one in-house signatory. Add, without breaking existing callers:

```ts
interface ReportTestProvenance {
  performedBy: string;                 // "Clinova Pathlabs"
  performedAt?: string;
  accreditationText?: string;          // only when accredited; text only, no logo
  reportedBy?: { name: string; qualification?: string; registration?: string; title?: string; signatureSrc?: string }[];
}
// on each test in the report request:
provenance?: ReportTestProvenance;
```

- Under each test with provenance, print one small line:
  "Performed at Clinova Pathlabs, Secunderabad · NABL accredited laboratory (MC-3860) · Reported by
  Dr …, MD (…)". Use `labelFor().text`, or build it from the parts.
- Signature block: when every test on a page comes from the same external PDF, print that PDF's
  medical signatory (name, qualification, registration, and the signature image from
  `external_signatures`) next to or instead of the in-house block, as the owner decides. Our own QC
  stamp and verifier stay. When a page mixes sources, print the per-test lines only.
- `signatureSrc` is a data URI the api builds from `external_signatures.png`, after checking rule 2:
  the report's `ResultProvenance.sourceSha256` must equal the signature row's `sourceSha256`.
- Keep the public package free of real signatures, as now: the images come from the api at render time.

## client (`@mgpl-diagnostics/client`)

Mirror the new operations and types (api rule 10): `importExternalReport`, `matchExternalReport`,
`applyExternalReport`, `rejectExternalReport`, `nameExternalSignature`, `externalReport(s)`,
`externalSignatories`. Then bump the client and its ref in `kits.json`.

## Tests (api `test/run.ts`, both databases)

Draw fictional partner PDFs with pdf-lib, using the same coordinates as `report-reader`'s
`scripts/make-fixtures.ts`. Do not copy real reports. Cover:

- import, then re-import (the second returns the same row);
- an unsupported PDF → `UNSUPPORTED_REPORT`;
- a booking mismatch → a warning;
- apply → `Report`s created with provenance, results equal to the extracted ones, and status unchanged
  until `verifyReport`;
- an accredited test gets the NABL label and an unmarked one does not;
- a signature is served only for its own PDF, and another report cannot get it;
- `nameExternalSignature` → re-extraction names the signer;
- permissions: no `reports.import` → forbidden; another org's ids → not found.

## Done when

- [ ] db-kit: the three collections or tables on both adapters, with migrations, released.
- [ ] auth-kit: `reports.import`, `signatories.manage` in `PERMISSIONS`, released.
- [ ] api: schema, controllers, services, job, limits, error codes; `npm run schema`,
      `npm run docs:reference`, `npm run llms`; tests green on PG + Mongo.
- [ ] report-kit: `provenance` on tests, per-test line, external signatory block; smoke-rendered with
      fictional data.
- [ ] client: operations and types; `kits.json` bumped.
- [ ] Docs: a new `api/docs` page for imports, linked from `docs/README.md`.

## File: docs/formats.md

# Report formats

How each supported lab lays out its PDF, as the parsers rely on it. Coordinates are PDF points on an A4
page (595 × 842), `y` measured from the top. Everything was observed on real reports; read this before
changing a parser, and re-run `npm run validate` and `npm run recall` on real reports after.

## Hy Patho Lab (`src/labs/hypatho.ts`)

Detected by "HY PATHO LAB" or "hypatholab" in the text.

| Region | Where | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Processed-at block | top right, x≈472, y 39–61 | "PROCESSED AT:" / "HY PATHO LAB" / city |
| Header | y 148–187, three columns starting x≈20 / 240 / 426 | `PT Name`, `Age : 26 Y \| Gender : FEMALE`, `Ref By Dr`, `Registered on`, `Booking Id`, `Received on`, `Barcode Id`, `Reported on`, `SAMPLE COLLECTED AT :`, `SAMPLE`, `INV` |
| Test title | centred, y≈216, only on the page where a test starts | e.g. "LIVER FUNCTION TESTS"; may start with "*" (kept as `mark`) |
| Table header | y≈243 (≈211 on continuation pages) | `TEST DESCRIPTION \| RESULT \| UNITS \| BIO. REF. RANGES [\| METHOD]` |
| Rows | name x≈20, result ≈246, unit ≈290–330, range ≈346–415 | one row per parameter, then `Method: X` at x≈20 |
| Notes | x≈25 | reference tables, interpretation, clinical significance |
| End | centred | `~~End of report~~` closes the test |
| Signature | image bottom right, x≈430, y≈720–750, about 120 × 74 | on the page where a test ends |
| Footer | y≈815 | `1 of 8` |

Quirks:

- `Reported on` prints its value on a separate text line about 3 pt **above** the label. The header
  parser attaches such an orphan `: value` to the label without a value in the same column.
- `SAMPLE COLLECTED AT :` has its value on the next line in the same column.
- Long names wrap onto a second line about 11 pt below (e.g. "(MCHC)"). A row normally comes about
  27 pt after the previous one.
- A test that continues on the next page has no title there. A `Method:` line at the top of the new page
  belongs to the last row of the previous page.
- Each page header has its own `SAMPLE` (EDTA, SERUM…), which becomes the test's `sampleType`.
- **The signer's name is only inside the signature image.** Naming needs the signature registry.
- No accreditation marks are printed.

## Clinova Pathlabs (`src/labs/clinova.ts`)

Detected by "Clinova" or a lab code like `CPL-XX-000`.

| Region | Where | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Title | centred, y≈96 (newer reports) | "LABORATORY TEST REPORT" |
| Header, left | labels x≈30, values x≈94–128 | `Patient Name`, `Age : 33 Year(s) Gender : Female`, `Sample ID`, `Sample Type`, `Patient ID`, `Ref. Doctor`, `Ref. Customer` |
| Header, right | labels x≈344, ":" x≈461, values x≈470 | `Lab Code`, `Sample Collection Date`, `Registration Date`, `Approved Date` (printed as two items) |
| Department | centred, just above the table header | "CLINICAL BIOCHEMISTRY", "HEMATOLOGY", "CLINICAL MICROBIOLOGY"… |
| Table header | | `Test Description \| Result \| Units \| Biological Reference Ranges` (x 32 / 310 / 372 / 414) |
| Rows | names x≈38–43, result 310, unit 369, range 426 | `(Method: X)` under a row or under a panel title |
| Interpretation | images x≈36, wide | between tests; they also end a panel |
| Notes | x≈33 | paragraphs, word-spaced across the width |
| End | centred | `--End of Report--` |
| Signatories | name y≈769, title y≈784; left x≈30, right x≈404 | signature image just above each (y≈727–736, about 116–134 × 21–22) |
| Accreditation | top centre (x≈286) or footer centre (x≈191) | ilac-MRA + NABL mark with the certificate number; legend "Tests marked with NABL symbol are accredited by NABL vide Certificate No.MC-3860" |
| Footer | | "Processed at : Clinova Pathlabs, Central Lab, …" (newer reports) |

Quirks:

- Each page prints **its own Sample ID, Sample Type and Approved Date**. They are kept per test
  (`sampleId`, `sampleType`, `reported`).
- Structure is told apart by layout, not by x position:
  - a short line with no result, followed by rows, is a panel title ("LIPID PROFILE");
  - inside an open panel, the same kind of line in the middle of a page is a group ("Erythrocyte Indices");
  - stacked headings (panel title, possibly wrapped, then a group, then rows) open the panel with the
    first group, as in "Complete Urine Examination (CUE)" followed by "PHYSICAL EXAMINATION";
  - a row with no panel open is a single-test section named after the row;
  - a paragraph or an interpretation image ends the panel.
- A panel continues across a page break only if the new page has the same Sample ID and starts with
  a row, not a heading.
- Culture reports have **no table header**: the department line starts the body, and default columns
  are used.
- Long text results wrap in the result column (antibiotic lists). Words broken in the middle of a comma
  list are joined back together.
- "." in the unit column means no unit.
- **NABL is marked per page**, not per row. In one 9-page report, only the 6 biochemistry pages carry
  the mark and legend; HbA1c, ESR and CBC do not. A test is `accredited: true` only when all its pages
  carry the mark. Clinova is the lab that holds the certificate: the mark says nothing about MGPL.

## Images seen

| What | How recognised |
| --- | --- |
| NABL / ilac-MRA mark (Clinova) | `ACCREDITATION_MARKS` in `src/registry.ts`, by pixel sha or perceptual hash |
| QR codes (both labs, one per report) | square images; never signatures |
| Logos, banners, interpretation charts | position and size; never signatures |
| Signatures | position (bottom band), size and aspect ratio; Clinova also pairs them with the name and title text below |

## Adding a lab

1. Collect a handful of its reports locally (never commit them).
2. Map the layout as in this file. The scratch tools in `scripts/` print aggregate stats only.
3. Add `src/labs/<lab>.ts` with `is<Lab>(doc)` and `parse<Lab>(doc) → LabParse`, add the lab to `LabId`,
   and wire it into `detectLab` and `extractReport`.
4. Draw a fictional report in the same layout in `scripts/make-fixtures.ts`, and add tests.
5. Run `npm run validate` and `npm run recall` on the real reports, and record the numbers in the README.

## File: llms.txt

# @mgpl-diagnostics/report-reader

> Reads partner-lab report PDFs (Hy Patho Lab, Clinova Pathlabs) into typed JSON: results (value, unit, range, method, H/L flag), patient, sample, dates, signatories with signature images and fingerprints, and NABL accreditation evidence per test. Uses the PDF text layer (exact, no OCR). Node ≥ 20.

Key facts for agents:
- `extractReport(pdfBytes, { signatures?, file? })` → `{ report, images }`; throws `UnsupportedReportError` for other PDFs.
- `labelFor(report, test)` → "Performed at … (NABL accredited, MC-…) · Reported by Dr …"; NABL appears only when `test.accredited === true`.
- Hy Patho prints the doctor's name only inside the signature image: pass `KnownSignature[]` (name + sha/dhash) from your database.
- A signature may only be shown next to results from the same PDF (`report.source.sha256`).
- Never commit real reports, extracted data or signatures; fixtures are fictional (`scripts/make-fixtures.ts`).
- Measured on 165 real reports: 3,888 / 3,888 printed numeric results extracted with the correct value and row.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): usage, output model, accuracy, rules
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): rules and map
- [docs/backend-integration.md](docs/backend-integration.md): api / db-kit / auth-kit / report-kit plan
- [docs/formats.md](docs/formats.md): layout of each lab's report

## Source

- [src/labs/hypatho.ts](src/labs/hypatho.ts), [src/labs/clinova.ts](src/labs/clinova.ts): parsers

## File: scripts/llms-full.mjs

````js
// Builds llms-full.txt: every doc and source file of the repo in one plain-text document for AI tools.
//   node scripts/llms-full.mjs "<title>" <file-or-folder> [file-or-folder …]
// Folders are walked recursively. Output order: README, AGENTS, docs, then the rest alphabetically.
// Skipped: build output, dependencies, lockfiles, generated files, binaries. Files over 150 KB are
// listed (path + size) instead of inlined. CI checks the file is up to date (`npm run llms` + git diff).
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { extname, join, relative } from "node:path";

const [title, ...inputs] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!title || !inputs.length) {
  console.error('usage: node scripts/llms-full.mjs "<title>" <file-or-folder> …');
  process.exit(1);
}

const TEXT = new Set([".ts", ".tsx", ".mts", ".cts", ".js", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".md", ".mdx", ".json", ".css", ".yml", ".yaml", ".txt", ".graphql", ".gql", ".sql", ".html"]);
const SKIP_DIRS = new Set(["node_modules", "dist", ".next", ".git", ".turbo", "coverage", "examples", ".pg-test"]);
const SKIP_FILES = /(^|\/)(package-lock\.json|pnpm-lock\.yaml|yarn\.lock|llms-full\.txt|[^/]*\.generated\.[^/]+|[^/]*\.log)$/;
const MAX = 150 * 1024;
const LANG = { ".ts": "ts", ".tsx": "tsx", ".mts": "ts", ".cts": "ts", ".js": "js", ".mjs": "js", ".cjs": "js", ".json": "json", ".css": "css", ".yml": "yaml", ".yaml": "yaml", ".graphql": "graphql", ".gql": "graphql", ".sql": "sql", ".html": "html" };

const posix = (p) => p.split("\\").join("/");
const files = new Set();
function walk(p) {
  const st = statSync(p);
  if (st.isDirectory()) {
    for (const name of readdirSync(p)) if (!SKIP_DIRS.has(name)) walk(join(p, name));
  } else if (TEXT.has(extname(p).toLowerCase()) && !SKIP_FILES.test(posix(p))) {
    files.add(posix(relative(".", p)));
  }
}
for (const input of inputs) walk(input);

const rank = (f) => (/^README\.md$/i.test(f) ? 0 : /^AGENTS\.md$/i.test(f) ? 1 : /^docs\//.test(f) ? 2 : 3);
const ordered = [...files].sort((a, b) => rank(a) - rank(b) || (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0));

const parts = [`# ${title} — full documentation and source\n\n> Generated by scripts/llms-full.mjs. Do not edit by hand. ${ordered.length} files.\n\n## Contents\n\n${ordered.map((f) => `- ${f}`).join("\n")}\n`];
const omitted = [];
for (const f of ordered) {
  // LF-normalised text, so Windows and Linux checkouts produce byte-identical output
  const body = readFileSync(f, "utf8").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").trim();
  const size = Buffer.byteLength(body);
  if (size > MAX) {
    omitted.push(`${f} (${(size / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB)`);
    parts.push(`\n\n---\n\n## File: ${f}\n\n_Omitted: ${(size / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB. Read the file directly._\n`);
    continue;
  }
  const lang = LANG[extname(f).toLowerCase()];
  const fence = body.includes("```") ? "````" : "```";
  parts.push(`\n\n---\n\n## File: ${f}\n\n${lang ? `${fence}${lang}\n${body}\n${fence}` : body}\n`);
}
const out = parts.join("");
writeFileSync("llms-full.txt", out);
console.log(`llms-full.txt: ${ordered.length} files, ${(out.length / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB${omitted.length ? `; omitted (too large): ${omitted.join(", ")}` : ""}`);
````

## File: scripts/make-fixtures.ts

```ts
/**
 * Synthetic test reports in the two supported layouts, written to test/fixtures/ (git-ignored).
 * Everything here is fictional: patients, doctors, signatures, registration and certificate numbers.
 * Never add real reports to this repo; validate on real ones locally with `npm run validate`.
 */
import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { PDFDocument, StandardFonts, type PDFFont, type PDFPage } from "pdf-lib";
import { toPng } from "../src/pdf";

const W = 595.28, H = 841.89;
const OUT = new URL("../test/fixtures/", import.meta.url);

/** A fake "signature": deterministic squiggle on a transparent background. */
function squiggle(w: number, h: number, seed: number) {
  const rgba = new Uint8ClampedArray(w * h * 4);
  let s = seed;
  const rnd = () => ((s = (s * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648) / 2147483648);
  const a = 0.25 + rnd() * 0.2, f = 2 + rnd() * 4, ph = rnd() * 6;
  for (let x = 4; x < w - 4; x++) {
    const y = Math.round(h / 2 + Math.sin((x / w) * Math.PI * f + ph) * h * a + Math.sin(x / 7) * h * 0.08);
    for (let t = -2; t <= 2; t++) {
      const yy = y + t;
      if (yy < 0 || yy >= h) continue;
      const j = (yy * w + x) * 4;
      rgba[j] = 20; rgba[j + 1] = 40; rgba[j + 2] = 140; rgba[j + 3] = 255;
    }
  }
  return toPng({ width: w, height: h, rgba });
}

async function page(doc: PDFDocument, font: PDFFont, bold: PDFFont) {
  const p = doc.addPage([W, H]);
  const text = (x: number, yTop: number, s: string, size = 7.5, f: PDFFont = font) => p.drawText(s, { x, y: H - yTop, size, font: f });
  return { p, text, bold };
}

async function image(doc: PDFDocument, p: PDFPage, png: Buffer, x: number, yTop: number, w: number, h: number) {
  const img = await doc.embedPng(png);
  p.drawImage(img, { x, y: H - yTop - h, width: w, height: h });
}

async function hypatho() {
  const doc = await PDFDocument.create();
  const font = await doc.embedFont(StandardFonts.Helvetica);
  const bold = await doc.embedFont(StandardFonts.HelveticaBold);
  const sig = squiggle(210, 130, 7);
  const header = (text: (x: number, y: number, s: string, size?: number, f?: PDFFont) => void, n: number, of: number) => {
    text(472, 39, "PROCESSED AT:", 8, bold);
    text(472, 50, "HY PATHO LAB", 8, bold);
    text(472, 61, "RAIPUR", 8, bold);
    text(20, 148, "PT Name"); text(70, 148, ": MR. TEST PATIENT"); text(240, 148, "Age"); text(308, 148, ": 40 Y | Gender : MALE"); text(426, 148, "SAMPLE COLLECTED AT :");
    text(20, 157, "Ref By Dr"); text(70, 157, ": SELF"); text(240, 157, "Registered on"); text(308, 157, ": 01-01-2026 09:00 AM"); text(426, 157, "DEMO COLLECTION CENTRE");
    text(20, 166, "Booking Id"); text(70, 166, ": 100001 DEMO - 1"); text(240, 166, "Received on"); text(308, 166, ": 01-01-2026 10:00 AM");
    text(308, 175, ": 01-01-2026 05:30 PM");
    text(20, 178, "Barcode Id"); text(70, 178, ": BC0001"); text(240, 178, "Reported on"); text(426, 178, "SAMPLE"); text(462, 178, ": SERUM");
    text(20, 187, "INV"); text(70, 187, ": DEMO PANEL");
    text(298, 815, `${n} of ${of}`);
  };
  const th = (text: (x: number, y: number, s: string, size?: number, f?: PDFFont) => void, y: number) => {
    text(20, y, "TEST DESCRIPTION", 8, bold); text(246, y, "RESULT", 8, bold); text(330, y, "UNITS", 8, bold); text(415, y, "BIO. REF. RANGES", 8, bold);
  };

  // page 1: a panel that continues on page 2
  let { p, text } = await page(doc, font, bold);
  header(text, 1, 3);
  text(222, 216, "COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT", 9, bold);
  th(text, 243);
  text(20, 262, "Hemoglobin"); text(246, 262, "9.50"); text(330, 262, "g/dL"); text(415, 262, "13 - 17");
  text(20, 271, "Method: SLS-Hemoglobin");
  text(20, 289, "Mean Corpuscular Hemoglobin Concentration"); text(246, 289, "35.80"); text(330, 289, "g/dl"); text(415, 289, "31.5 - 34.5");
  text(20, 300, "(MCHC)");
  text(20, 310, "Method: Calculated");
  text(20, 328, "DIFFERENTIAL COUNT", 7.5, bold);
  text(20, 346, "Neutrophils"); text(246, 346, "62"); text(330, 346, "%"); text(415, 346, "40 - 80");
  text(20, 355, "Method: Flow Cytometry");
  text(20, 790, "Platelet Count"); text(246, 790, "120"); text(330, 790, "10^3/uL"); text(415, 790, "150 - 410");

  // page 2: continuation (no title), method line carried over, end of report, signature
  ({ p, text } = await page(doc, font, bold));
  header(text, 2, 3);
  th(text, 211);
  text(20, 225, "Method: Electrical Impedance");
  text(20, 243, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR)"); text(246, 243, "34"); text(330, 243, "mm at end of Ist hr"); text(415, 243, "0 - 20");
  text(236, 300, "~~End of report~~");
  await image(doc, p, sig, 430, 720, 120, 74);

  // page 3: a marked single test with narrative notes
  ({ p, text } = await page(doc, font, bold));
  header(text, 3, 3);
  text(223, 216, "* THYROID PROFILE", 9, bold);
  th(text, 243);
  text(20, 262, "THYROID STIMULATING HORMONE (TSH)"); text(246, 262, "6.20"); text(330, 262, "uIU/ml"); text(415, 262, "0.35 - 5.5");
  text(20, 271, "Method: CLIA");
  text(25, 300, "Interpretation: values vary with time of day; repeat if clinically indicated.");
  text(236, 340, "~~End of report~~");
  await image(doc, p, sig, 430, 720, 120, 74);

  return doc.save();
}

async function clinova() {
  const doc = await PDFDocument.create();
  const font = await doc.embedFont(StandardFonts.Helvetica);
  const bold = await doc.embedFont(StandardFonts.HelveticaBold);
  const left = squiggle(150, 80, 11), right = squiggle(250, 68, 23);

  const make = async (n: number, of: number, sampleId: string, sampleType: string, dept: string, accredited: boolean) => {
    const { p, text } = await page(doc, font, bold);
    text(242, 96, "LABORATORY TEST REPORT", 10, bold);
    text(30, 117, "Patient Name"); text(94, 117, "Mr DEMO PERSON", 8, bold);
    text(30, 131, "Age : 35 Year(s) Gender : Male");
    text(344, 141, "Lab Code"); text(461, 141, ":"); text(470, 141, "CPL-XX-001");
    text(30, 145, "Sample ID"); text(119, 145, ":"); text(128, 145, sampleId);
    text(344, 156, "Sample Collection Date"); text(461, 156, ":"); text(470, 156, "2026-01-02 08:15");
    text(30, 159, "Sample Type"); text(119, 159, ":"); text(128, 159, sampleType);
    text(30, 171, "Patient ID"); text(119, 171, ":"); text(128, 171, "900001"); text(344, 171, "Registration Date"); text(461, 171, ":"); text(470, 171, "2026-01-02 10:00");
    text(30, 186, "Ref. Doctor"); text(119, 186, ":"); text(344, 186, "Approved"); text(389, 186, "Date"); text(461, 186, ":"); text(470, 186, `2026-01-02 1${n}:30`);
    text(30, 200, "Ref. Customer"); text(119, 200, ":"); text(128, 200, "DEMO COLLECTION CENTRE");
    text(236, 220, dept, 8, bold);
    text(32, 242, "Test Description", 8, bold); text(310, 242, "Result", 8, bold); text(372, 242, "Units", 8, bold); text(414, 242, "Biological Reference Ranges", 8, bold);
    await image(doc, p, left, 29, 736, 116, 21);
    await image(doc, p, right, 404, 735, 134, 22);
    text(30, 769, "Demo Manager"); text(404, 769, "Dr Demo Pathologist, MD");
    text(30, 784, "Manager Lab Operations"); text(404, 784, "Consultant Pathologist (XYMC1234/2020)");
    text(30, 808, "This is an electronically authenticated report.", 5);
    text(543, 808, `Page ${n} of ${of}`, 5);
    if (accredited) text(30, 822, "Tests marked with NABL symbol are accredited by NABL vide Certificate No.MC-9999", 5);
    text(30, 830, "Processed at : Clinova Pathlabs, Demo Central Lab, Demo City - 000000", 5);
    return text;
  };

  let text = await make(1, 2, "S-001", "Serum", "CLINICAL BIOCHEMISTRY", true);
  text(39, 262, "LIPID PROFILE");
  text(39, 277, "Cholesterol - Total"); text(310, 277, "245"); text(369, 277, "mg/dL"); text(426, 277, "<200 - Desirable");
  text(39, 285, "(Method: CHOD-PAP)", 6);
  text(426, 289, "200-239 - Borderline risk");
  text(426, 300, ">240 - High risk");
  text(39, 311, "Cholesterol - HDL"); text(310, 311, "35"); text(369, 311, "mg/dL"); text(426, 311, "40 - 60");
  text(39, 320, "(Method: Enzymatic Colorimetric)", 6);
  text(33, 360, "HDL cholesterol below 40 mg/dL is a cardiovascular risk factor. Correlate clinically with other findings.");

  text = await make(2, 2, "S-002", "WB EDTA", "HEMATOLOGY", false);
  text(39, 260, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR)"); text(310, 260, "30"); text(369, 260, "mm/Hour"); text(426, 260, "<= 20");
  text(39, 269, "(Method: Westergren)", 6);
  text(248, 500, "--End of Report--");

  return doc.save();
}

mkdirSync(OUT, { recursive: true });
writeFileSync(new URL("hypatho-demo.pdf", OUT), await hypatho());
writeFileSync(new URL("clinova-demo.pdf", OUT), await clinova());
console.log("fixtures written to test/fixtures/");

## File: scripts/recall.ts

```ts
/**
 * npm run recall -- <folder|list.txt> [--signatures known.json]
 * Independent cross-check of the table parser: every numeric value printed in a table's RESULT column
 * (found directly from text positions, without the parser's row logic) must appear as an extracted
 * result of the same report, with the same value and its row's name. Prints aggregate counts only.
 */
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { extractReport, readPdf } from "../src/index";
import { headerColumns } from "../src/table";

const input = process.argv[2];
if (!input) throw new Error("usage: recall <folder|list.txt>");
const files = statSync(input).isDirectory()
  ? readdirSync(input).filter((f) => /\.pdf$/i.test(f)).map((f) => join(input, f))
  : readFileSync(input, "utf8").split(/\r?\n/).filter(Boolean).map((f) => join(process.env.REPORTS_DIR ?? dirname(input), f));

let printed = 0, found = 0, wrongName = 0, extracted = 0, unmatchedExtracted = 0;
const missReports = new Set<string>();
for (const f of files) {
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(readFileSync(f));
  const doc = await readPdf(bytes, { images: false });
  const { report } = await extractReport(bytes);
  const params = report.tests.flatMap((t) => t.parameters);
  extracted += params.length;
  const pool = params.map((p) => ({ v: p.value, n: p.name, used: false }));
  for (const page of doc.pages) {
    let cols: ReturnType<typeof headerColumns> = null;
    for (const line of page.lines) {
      const h = headerColumns(line);
      if (h) { cols = h; continue; }
      if (!cols || line.y > page.height * 0.87) continue;
      const res = line.items.filter((i) => Math.abs(i.x - cols!.result) <= 8);
      const name = line.items.filter((i) => i.x < cols!.result - 8).map((i) => i.s).join(" ").trim();
      for (const r of res) {
        if (!/^[<>]?\s*\d+(\.\d+)?\s*[HL*]?$/.test(r.s) || !name || line.items[0]!.x > cols.result) continue;
        printed++;
        const value = r.s.replace(/\s*[HL*]$/, "").trim();
        const hit = pool.find((p) => !p.used && p.v === value && p.n.startsWith(name.slice(0, 12)))
          ?? pool.find((p) => !p.used && p.v === value);
        if (hit) {
          hit.used = true;
          found++;
          if (!hit.n.startsWith(name.slice(0, 12))) wrongName++;
        } else missReports.add(f);
      }
    }
  }
  unmatchedExtracted += pool.filter((p) => !p.used && /^[<>]?\d/.test(p.v)).length;
}
console.log(`printed numeric results: ${printed}`);
console.log(`extracted with same value: ${found} (${((found / printed) * 100).toFixed(2)}%)`);
console.log(`  of which under a different name: ${wrongName}`);
console.log(`reports with a missed value: ${missReports.size} / ${files.length}`);
console.log(`extracted numeric results not seen by the cross-check: ${unmatchedExtracted} (of ${extracted} extracted)`);
```

## File: scripts/validate.ts

```ts
/**
 * npm run validate -- <folder-or-list.txt> [--signatures known.json] [--dump dir]
 * Runs the extractor over real reports and prints AGGREGATE quality stats only (no patient data), so the
 * output can be shared. --dump writes each JSON to a local folder for inspection (keep it git-ignored).
 */
import { mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { basename, dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { extractReport, type KnownSignature } from "../src/index";

const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const opt = (n: string) => {
  const i = args.indexOf(n);
  return i >= 0 ? args.splice(i, 2)[1] : undefined;
};
const sigFile = opt("--signatures");
const dump = opt("--dump");
const signatures: KnownSignature[] = sigFile ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(sigFile, "utf8")) : [];
const input = args[0];
if (!input) throw new Error("usage: validate <folder|list.txt> [--signatures f] [--dump dir]");
const files = statSync(input).isDirectory()
  ? readdirSync(input).filter((f) => /\.pdf$/i.test(f)).map((f) => join(input, f))
  : readFileSync(input, "utf8").split(/\r?\n/).filter(Boolean).map((f) => join(process.env.REPORTS_DIR ?? dirname(input), f));
if (dump) mkdirSync(dump, { recursive: true });

const count = new Map<string, number>();
const inc = (k: string, n = 1) => count.set(k, (count.get(k) ?? 0) + n);
const t0 = performance.now();
for (const f of files) {
  try {
    const { report: r } = await extractReport(new Uint8Array(readFileSync(f)), { signatures });
    const L = r.source.lab;
    inc(`${L} reports`);
    inc(`${L} pages`, r.source.pages);
    inc(`${L} tests`, r.tests.length);
    inc(`${L} results`, r.tests.reduce((n, t) => n + t.parameters.length, 0));
    for (const k of ["name", "ageYears", "sex"] as const) if (r.patient[k] !== undefined) inc(`${L} has patient.${k}`);
    for (const k of ["registered", "collected", "received", "reported"] as const) if (r.dates[k]) inc(`${L} has dates.${k}`);
    if (r.dates.reported && !/^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d$/.test(r.dates.reported)) inc(`${L} unparsed reported date`);
    if (r.tests.some((t) => t.signedBy.some((id) => r.signatories.find((s) => s.id === id)?.medical))) inc(`${L} has medical signer`);
    if (r.tests.some((t) => !t.signedBy.length)) inc(`${L} reports with an unsigned test`);
    if (r.accreditation.length) inc(`${L} with NABL evidence`);
    for (const t of r.tests) {
      if (!t.parameters.length) inc(`${L} tests without results`);
      if (t.accredited === true) inc(`${L} tests accredited`);
      if (t.accredited === false) inc(`${L} tests not marked`);
      for (const p of t.parameters) {
        if (p.flag) inc(`${L} flagged results`);
        if (!p.unit && /^-?\d/.test(p.value)) inc(`${L} numeric results without unit`);
        if (!p.range) inc(`${L} results without range`);
        if (p.method) inc(`${L} results with method`);
      }
    }
    for (const s of r.signatories) inc(`${L} signer: ${s.name ?? `UNNAMED ${s.id}`} [${s.role}${s.medical ? ", medical" : ""}]`);
    for (const w of r.warnings) inc(`${L} warning: ${w.replace(/\d+/g, "#").replace(/"[^"]*"/g, '"…"').slice(0, 90)}`);
    if (dump) writeFileSync(join(dump, basename(f).replace(/\.pdf$/i, ".json")), JSON.stringify(r, null, 2));
  } catch (e) {
    inc(`FAILED: ${(e as Error).message.slice(0, 80)}`);
  }
}
for (const [k, v] of [...count].sort((a, b) => (a[0] < b[0] ? -1 : 1))) console.log(String(v).padStart(6), k);
console.log(`${files.length} files in ${((performance.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(1)} s`);
```

## File: src/cli.ts

```ts
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * report-reader <report.pdf …> [--out dir] [--signatures known.json]
 * Writes <out>/<name>.json and <out>/signatures/<id>.png for each report. Default out: ./private/extracted
 * (git-ignored: extracted reports contain patient data and real signatures).
 */
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { basename, join } from "node:path";
import { extractReport, toPng, type KnownSignature } from "./index";

const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const opt = (name: string) => {
  const i = args.indexOf(name);
  return i >= 0 ? args.splice(i, 2)[1] : undefined;
};
const out = opt("--out") ?? "private/extracted";
const sigFile = opt("--signatures");
const signatures: KnownSignature[] = sigFile ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(sigFile, "utf8")) : [];
if (!args.length || args.includes("--help")) {
  console.log("usage: report-reader <report.pdf …> [--out dir] [--signatures known.json]");
  process.exit(args.length ? 0 : 1);
}

mkdirSync(join(out, "signatures"), { recursive: true });
let failed = 0;
for (const file of args) {
  try {
    const { report, images } = await extractReport(new Uint8Array(readFileSync(file)), { file: basename(file), signatures });
    for (const s of report.signatories) {
      const img = images.get(s.id);
      if (!img) continue;
      s.signature.file = join("signatures", `${s.id}.png`).split("\\").join("/");
      writeFileSync(join(out, s.signature.file), toPng(img));
    }
    const name = basename(file).replace(/\.pdf$/i, "");
    writeFileSync(join(out, `${name}.json`), JSON.stringify(report, null, 2));
    const params = report.tests.reduce((n, t) => n + t.parameters.length, 0);
    console.log(`${basename(file)}: ${report.source.lab}, ${report.tests.length} tests, ${params} results, ${report.signatories.length} signatories${report.warnings.length ? `, ${report.warnings.length} warnings` : ""}`);
  } catch (e) {
    failed++;
    console.error(`${basename(file)}: ${(e as Error).message}`);
  }
}
process.exit(failed ? 1 : 0);
```

## File: src/index.ts

```ts
/**
 * @mgpl-diagnostics/report-reader — read a partner lab's report PDF into typed JSON.
 *
 *   const { report, images } = await extractReport(pdfBytes, { signatures: knownFromDb });
 *
 * Supported: Hy Patho Lab, Clinova Pathlabs. Uses the PDF's text layer (exact); no OCR.
 */
import { readPdf, type PdfDoc } from "./pdf";
import { accreditationMark, knownSignature } from "./registry";
import { isClinova, parseClinova } from "./labs/clinova";
import { isHypatho, parseHypatho } from "./labs/hypatho";
import type { LabParse } from "./labs/common";
import { isMedical, parseSignatoryText, roleOf } from "./text";
import type { Accreditation, ExtractedReport, ExtractOptions, LabId, Signatory, SignatureImages } from "./types";

export * from "./types";
export { readPdf, toPng, dhash, hamming } from "./pdf";
export type { PdfDoc, PdfPage, PdfImage, Line, TextItem } from "./pdf";
export { ACCREDITATION_MARKS } from "./registry";
export { labelFor, type ProvenanceLabel } from "./label";

export class UnsupportedReportError extends Error {
  constructor(message = "Not a Hy Patho Lab or Clinova Pathlabs report") {
    super(message);
    this.name = "UnsupportedReportError";
  }
}

/** Which lab printed this PDF, or null. */
export function detectLab(doc: PdfDoc): LabId | null {
  if (isHypatho(doc)) return "hypatho";
  if (isClinova(doc)) return "clinova";
  return null;
}

const NABL_TEXT = /\bNABL\b/i;
const CERT = /\b(MC|TC|CC)\s*-\s*?(\d{3,6})\b/;

export async function extractReport(
  data: Uint8Array,
  opts: ExtractOptions = {},
): Promise<{ report: ExtractedReport; images: SignatureImages }> {
  const doc = await readPdf(data, { images: true });
  const lab = detectLab(doc);
  if (!lab) throw new UnsupportedReportError();
  const parsed: LabParse = lab === "hypatho" ? parseHypatho(doc) : parseClinova(doc);
  const warnings = [...parsed.warnings];
  const images: SignatureImages = new Map();

  // signatories, merged across pages by signature fingerprint (or by printed name when there is no image)
  const byId = new Map<string, Signatory>();
  for (const s of parsed.signatures) {
    const known = s.image ? knownSignature(s.image, opts.signatures) : undefined;
    const text = parseSignatoryText(s.nameLine, s.titleLine);
    const id = s.image?.sha ?? `text:${(text.name ?? text.title ?? "unknown").toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-")}`;
    let sig = byId.get(id);
    if (!sig) {
      const name = text.name ?? known?.name ?? null;
      if (known && text.name && !sameName(known.name, text.name))
        warnings.push(`signature ${id} is registered to "${known.name}" but printed beside "${text.name}"`);
      sig = {
        id,
        name,
        qualification: text.qualification ?? known?.qualification,
        registration: text.registration ?? known?.registration,
        title: text.title ?? known?.title,
        role: known?.role ?? roleOf(text.title, text.qualification, name ?? undefined),
        medical: false,
        signature: s.image
          ? { sha: s.image.sha, dhash: s.image.dhash, width: s.image.width, height: s.image.height }
          : { sha: "", dhash: "", width: 0, height: 0 },
        source: text.name ? "text" : known ? "registry" : "unknown",
        pages: [],
      };
      if (sig.role === "unknown") sig.role = roleOf(sig.title, sig.qualification, sig.name ?? undefined);
      sig.medical = isMedical(sig.name, sig.qualification);
      for (const k of Object.keys(sig) as (keyof Signatory)[]) if (sig[k] === undefined) delete sig[k];
      byId.set(id, sig);
      if (s.image && opts.signatureImages !== false) images.set(id, { width: s.image.width, height: s.image.height, rgba: s.image.rgba });
      if (!sig.name) warnings.push(`unnamed signature ${id} on page ${s.page}: add it to your signature registry`);
    }
    if (!sig.pages.includes(s.page)) sig.pages.push(s.page);
  }
  const signatories = [...byId.values()];

  // accreditation evidence per page: the mark (image) and/or the legend (text)
  const accreditation: Accreditation[] = [];
  const nablPages = new Set<number>();
  for (const page of doc.pages) {
    const evidence: ("logo" | "text")[] = [];
    let certificate: string | undefined;
    const mark = page.images.map(accreditationMark).find(Boolean);
    if (mark) {
      evidence.push("logo");
      certificate = mark.certificate;
    }
    const legend = page.lines.find((l) => NABL_TEXT.test(l.text));
    if (legend) {
      evidence.push("text");
      const c = legend.text.match(CERT);
      if (c) certificate = `${c[1]}-${c[2]}`;
    }
    if (!evidence.length) continue;
    nablPages.add(page.number);
    const a = accreditation.find((x) => x.certificate === certificate);
    if (a) {
      a.pages.push(page.number);
      for (const e of evidence) if (!a.evidence.includes(e)) a.evidence.push(e);
    } else accreditation.push({ body: "NABL", ...(certificate ? { certificate } : {}), evidence, pages: [page.number] });
  }

  for (const t of parsed.tests) {
    t.signedBy = signatories.filter((s) => s.pages.some((p) => t.pages.includes(p))).map((s) => s.id);
    if (nablPages.size) t.accredited = t.pages.length > 0 && t.pages.every((p) => nablPages.has(p));
    if (!t.parameters.length && !t.notes) warnings.push(`test "${t.name}" has no results`);
  }
  if (!parsed.tests.length) warnings.push("no tests found");

  const report: ExtractedReport = {
    source: {
      ...(opts.file ? { file: opts.file } : {}),
      sha256: doc.sha256,
      lab,
      labName: parsed.labName,
      ...(parsed.processedAt ? { processedAt: parsed.processedAt } : {}),
      pages: doc.pages.length,
    },
    patient: clean(parsed.patient),
    sample: clean(parsed.sample),
    dates: clean(parsed.dates),
    tests: parsed.tests,
    signatories,
    accreditation,
    warnings,
  };
  return { report, images };
}

const norm = (s: string) => s.toLowerCase().replace(/^dr\.?\s*/, "").replace(/[^a-z]+/g, " ").trim();
const sameName = (a: string, b: string) => norm(a) === norm(b) || norm(a).includes(norm(b)) || norm(b).includes(norm(a));

function clean<T extends object>(o: T): T {
  for (const k of Object.keys(o) as (keyof T)[]) if (o[k] === undefined || o[k] === "") delete o[k];
  return o;
}
```

## File: src/label.ts

```ts
/**
 * Provenance label for one test, for printing on our own report design: which lab performed it, which
 * doctor reported it, and whether the performing lab's NABL mark applies to it.
 *
 * Rules this function enforces (see AGENTS.md):
 * - Accreditation belongs to the PERFORMING lab and only to tests its report marks; never to MGPL.
 * - Only medical signatories (pathologist / biochemist / microbiologist consultants) are "reported by".
 * - A signature image may only be shown next to results from the same source PDF (sourceSha256).
 */
import type { ExtractedReport, Signatory, TestSection } from "./types";

export interface ProvenanceLabel {
  performedBy: string;
  performedAt?: string;
  reportedBy: Pick<Signatory, "id" | "name" | "qualification" | "registration" | "title" | "role">[];
  /** present only when the report marks this test with the performing lab's NABL mark */
  accreditation?: { body: "NABL"; certificate?: string; text: string };
  /** the PDF these results and signatures came from */
  sourceSha256: string;
  /** one line, e.g. "Performed at Clinova Pathlabs (NABL accredited, MC-3860) · Reported by Dr X, MD" */
  text: string;
}

export function labelFor(report: ExtractedReport, test: TestSection): ProvenanceLabel {
  const signers = report.signatories.filter((s) => test.signedBy.includes(s.id));
  const medical = signers.filter((s) => s.medical);
  const reportedBy = medical.map(({ id, name, qualification, registration, title, role }) => ({ id, name, qualification, registration, title, role }));
  const cert = test.accredited ? report.accreditation.find((a) => a.pages.some((p) => test.pages.includes(p))) : undefined;
  const accreditation = test.accredited
    ? {
        body: "NABL" as const,
        certificate: cert?.certificate,
        text: `Performed at a NABL accredited laboratory${cert?.certificate ? ` (Certificate No. ${cert.certificate})` : ""}`,
      }
    : undefined;
  const who = reportedBy
    .filter((r) => r.name)
    .map((r) => [r.name, r.qualification].filter(Boolean).join(", ") + (r.registration ? ` (${r.registration})` : ""))
    .join("; ");
  const text = [
    `Performed at ${report.source.labName}${accreditation ? ` (NABL accredited${cert?.certificate ? `, ${cert.certificate}` : ""})` : ""}`,
    who && `Reported by ${who}`,
  ]
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join(" · ");
  return {
    performedBy: report.source.labName,
    ...(report.source.processedAt ? { performedAt: report.source.processedAt } : {}),
    reportedBy,
    ...(accreditation ? { accreditation } : {}),
    sourceSha256: report.source.sha256,
    text,
  };
}
```

## File: src/labs/clinova.ts

```ts
/**
 * Clinova Pathlabs reports ("LABORATORY TEST REPORT", lab code CPL-…).
 *
 * Page: header with patient fields left (x≈30) and dates right (x≈347, ":" at 461); a centred department
 * ("CLINICAL BIOCHEMISTRY"); a table "Test Description | Result | Units | Biological Reference Ranges";
 * panels ("LIPID PROFILE") or single-test rows; "(Method: X)" under rows and panel names; multi-line
 * ranges in the range column; interpretation images between tests; "--End of Report--".
 * Bottom: signatories, left (x≈30) and right (x≈404), each a signature image above a name line and a
 * title line. Accredited pages carry the ilac-MRA/NABL mark and the legend
 * "Tests marked with NABL symbol are accredited by NABL vide Certificate No.MC-3860".
 * Each page header prints its own Sample ID, Sample Type and Approved Date.
 */
import type { Line, PdfDoc, PdfImage } from "../pdf";
import { accreditationMark, isSquare } from "../registry";
import { cells, headerColumns, makeParameter, METHOD_LINE, type Columns } from "../table";
import { emptyReport, field, headerFields, isoDate, parseAge, parseSex, splitTitle, uniq } from "../text";
import type { Parameter, TestSection } from "../types";
import { FOOTER_PAGE, joinWrapped, type LabParse } from "./common";

export const isClinova = (doc: PdfDoc) =>
  doc.pages.slice(0, 2).some((p) => p.lines.some((l) => /clinova|\bCPL-[A-Z]{2}-\d+/i.test(l.text)));

const LABELS = [
  /^Patient\s*Name\b\s*:?/i,
  /^Age\b\s*:?/i,
  /^Sample\s*ID\b\s*:?/i,
  /^Sample\s*Type\b\s*:?/i,
  /^Patient\s*ID\b\s*:?/i,
  /^Ref\.?\s*Doctor\b\s*:?/i,
  /^Ref\.?\s*Customer\b\s*:?/i,
  /^Lab\s*Code\b\s*:?/i,
  /^Sample\s*Collection\s*Date\b\s*:?/i,
  /^Registration\s*Date\b\s*:?/i,
  /^(?:Approved|Reported|Authori[sz]ed)\s*Date\b\s*:?/i,
];

const END = /-{2,}\s*End\s*of\s*Report\s*-{2,}/i;
const BOILERPLATE = /^(this is an electronically|note\s*:|tests marked with|processed at|page \d+ of)/i;

export function parseClinova(doc: PdfDoc): LabParse {
  const out: LabParse = { lab: "clinova", labName: "Clinova Pathlabs", ...emptyReport(), signatures: [] };
  const colls: string[] = [], regs: string[] = [], apprs: string[] = [];
  let panel: TestSection | null = null; // open panel: later rows join it
  let cur: TestSection | null = null; // last section, for methods / ranges / notes
  let last: (Parameter & { group?: string }) | null = null;
  let group: string | undefined, groupMethod: string | undefined;
  const inherited = new WeakSet<Parameter>(); // method taken from the group / panel, replaced by the row's own
  let prevSampleId: string | undefined;

  for (const page of doc.pages) {
    const sigTop = page.height * 0.88;
    const all = page.lines.filter((l) => !FOOTER_PAGE.test(l.text));
    for (const l of all) {
      const m = l.text.match(/Processed\s*at\s*:\s*(.+)$/i);
      if (m && !out.processedAt) out.processedAt = m[1]!.trim();
    }
    let thIdx = all.findIndex((l) => l.y < sigTop && headerColumns(l));
    let cols: Columns | null = thIdx >= 0 ? headerColumns(all[thIdx]!) : null;
    let deptLine = thIdx > 0 && all[thIdx - 1]!.items[0]!.x > 150 ? all[thIdx - 1] : undefined;
    if (thIdx < 0) {
      // no column header (e.g. culture reports): the centred department line starts the body
      const d = all.findIndex((l) => l.y > 200 && l.y < sigTop && l.items.length === 1 && l.items[0]!.x > 150 && !/[a-z]/.test(l.text));
      if (d >= 0) {
        deptLine = all[d];
        thIdx = d; // body starts after it
        cols = { name: 32, result: 300 };
      }
    }
    const headLines = all.slice(0, deptLine ? all.indexOf(deptLine) : thIdx >= 0 ? thIdx : 0).filter((l) => l.y > 100);

    const f = headerFields(headLines, [340], LABELS);
    if (!out.patient.name) {
      const { title, name } = splitTitle(field(f, /patient\s*name/i));
      const ageRaw = field(f, /^age/i);
      const [ageText, sex] = (ageRaw ?? "").split(/\s*Gender\s*:?\s*/i);
      Object.assign(out.patient, { name, title, ...parseAge(ageText), sex: parseSex(sex), patientId: field(f, /patient\s*id/i) });
      out.sample.labCode = field(f, /lab\s*code/i);
      out.sample.referredBy = field(f, /doctor/i);
      out.sample.customer = field(f, /customer/i);
    }
    const sampleId = field(f, /sample\s*id/i);
    const sampleType = field(f, /sample\s*type/i);
    const reported = isoDate(field(f, /approved|reported|authori/i));
    out.sample.sampleIds.push(sampleId ?? "");
    colls.push(isoDate(field(f, /collection/i)) ?? "");
    regs.push(isoDate(field(f, /registration/i)) ?? "");
    apprs.push(reported ?? "");
    const department = deptLine?.text;

    // signatories: name + title lines per column, the signature image just above
    const sigLines = all.filter((l) => l.y >= sigTop && l.y < page.height - 45 && !BOILERPLATE.test(l.text));
    const columns = new Map<"left" | "right", Line["items"]>();
    for (const l of sigLines) for (const it of l.items) {
      const k = it.x < page.width / 2 ? "left" : "right";
      columns.set(k, [...(columns.get(k) ?? []), it]);
    }
    const sigImages = page.images.filter(
      (im) => im.box.y > page.height * 0.82 && im.box.w <= 200 && !isSquare(im) && !accreditationMark(im),
    );
    const used = new Set<PdfImage>();
    for (const items of columns.values()) {
      const rows: { y: number; s: string }[] = [];
      for (const it of items.sort((a, b) => a.y - b.y || a.x - b.x)) {
        const row = rows[rows.length - 1];
        if (row && Math.abs(row.y - it.y) <= 2.5) row.s += ` ${it.s}`;
        else rows.push({ y: it.y, s: it.s });
      }
      const x0 = Math.min(...items.map((i) => i.x));
      const image = sigImages.find((im) => !used.has(im) && Math.abs(im.box.x - x0) <= 40);
      if (image) used.add(image);
      const [a, b] = rows.map((r) => r.s.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim());
      out.signatures.push(
        b !== undefined
          ? { page: page.number, image, nameLine: a, titleLine: b }
          : /^dr\.?\s/i.test(a ?? "") ? { page: page.number, image, nameLine: a } : { page: page.number, image, titleLine: a },
      );
    }

    if (!cols) continue;
    const bodyEnd = all.findIndex((l, i) => i > thIdx && l.y >= sigTop);
    const body = all.slice(thIdx + 1, bodyEnd < 0 ? undefined : bodyEnd).filter((l) => !BOILERPLATE.test(l.text));
    const breaks = page.images.filter((im) => im.box.w > 250 && im.box.y > all[thIdx]!.y && im.box.y < sigTop).map((im) => im.box.y);
    const paramX = cols.name + 4;
    const cellOf = (l: Line) => cells(l, cols);
    const isRow = (l: Line | undefined) => {
      if (!l || l.items[0]!.x < paramX) return false;
      const c = cellOf(l);
      return !!c.result && !!c.name && !METHOD_LINE.test(c.name);
    };
    const isMethod = (l: Line) => {
      const c = cellOf(l);
      return !c.result && METHOD_LINE.test(c.name);
    };
    const sameSample = !!sampleId && sampleId === prevSampleId;
    if (!sameSample) panel = null;
    prevSampleId = sampleId;

    let prevKind: "row" | "heading" | "group" | "other" = "other";
    let prevY = all[thIdx]!.y;
    let firstRow = true;
    const touch = (s: TestSection) => {
      if (!s.pages.includes(page.number)) s.pages.push(page.number);
    };
    const newSection = (name: string): TestSection => {
      const s: TestSection = { name, department, sampleType, sampleId, reported, parameters: [], pages: [page.number], signedBy: [] };
      Object.keys(s).forEach((k) => (s as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)[k] === undefined && delete (s as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)[k]);
      out.tests.push(s);
      return s;
    };

    for (let i = 0; i < body.length; i++) {
      const line = body[i]!;
      if (breaks.some((y) => y > prevY && y < line.y)) panel = null; // interpretation image ends a panel
      const lastY = prevY;
      prevY = line.y;
      if (END.test(line.text)) {
        panel = cur = null;
        last = null;
        continue;
      }
      const c = cellOf(line);
      if (isMethod(line)) {
        const m = c.name.match(METHOD_LINE)![1]!.trim();
        if (prevKind === "row" && last && (!last.method || inherited.has(last))) {
          last.method = m;
          inherited.delete(last);
        }
        else if (prevKind === "group") groupMethod = m;
        else if (prevKind === "heading" && panel) panel.method = m;
        if (c.range && last) last.range = last.range ? `${last.range}\n${c.range}` : c.range;
        continue;
      }
      if (isRow(line)) {
        if (!panel) group = groupMethod = undefined; // a standalone test row is never in a group
        const p: Parameter & { group?: string } = { ...makeParameter(c.name, c), ...(group ? { group } : {}) };
        const fallback = groupMethod ?? (panel ? panel.method : undefined);
        if (!p.method && fallback) {
          p.method = fallback;
          inherited.add(p);
        }
        if (panel) {
          panel.parameters.push(p);
          touch(panel);
          cur = panel;
        } else {
          cur = newSection(c.name);
          cur.parameters.push(p);
        }
        last = p;
        prevKind = "row";
        firstRow = false;
        continue;
      }
      if (!c.name && !c.result && c.range && last) {
        last.range = last.range ? `${last.range}\n${c.range}` : c.range;
        continue;
      }
      if (!c.name && c.result && !c.unit && !c.range && last && prevKind === "row") {
        last.value = joinWrapped(last.value, c.result); // a long text result wrapped onto the next line
        continue;
      }
      const next = body.slice(i + 1).find((l) => !isMethod(l));
      // a heading is short, does not end a sentence, and is not the tail of a paragraph just above
      const paragraphTail = prevKind === "other" && line.y - lastY <= 13.5 && line.items[0]!.x < paramX;
      const onlyName = !c.result && !c.unit && !c.range && line.text.length <= 80 && !/[.:;]$/.test(c.name) && !paragraphTail;
      if (onlyName && !isRow(next)) {
        // stacked headings: panel title (maybe wrapped) [+ method], then a group heading, then rows
        const chain: Line[] = [line];
        let j = i + 1;
        for (; j < body.length; j++) {
          const l = body[j]!;
          if (isMethod(l)) continue;
          const lc = cellOf(l);
          if (lc.result || lc.unit || lc.range || l.text.length > 80) break;
          chain.push(l);
        }
        if (chain.length >= 2 && isRow(body[j])) {
          const titleLines = chain.slice(0, -1);
          const opened = newSection(titleLines.map((l) => cellOf(l).name).join(" ").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim());
          panel = cur = opened;
          group = groupMethod = undefined;
          for (let k = i + 1; k < body.indexOf(chain[chain.length - 1]!); k++)
            if (isMethod(body[k]!)) opened.method = cellOf(body[k]!).name.match(METHOD_LINE)![1]!.trim();
          i = body.indexOf(chain[chain.length - 1]!) - 1; // the group heading is handled next
          prevKind = "heading";
          firstRow = false;
          continue;
        }
      }
      if (onlyName && isRow(next)) {
        // a heading opens a new panel, except right under a panel title or mid-page inside a panel (a group)
        const justOpened = !!panel && !panel.parameters.length && prevKind === "heading";
        if (panel && (justOpened || (panel.parameters.length && !firstRow))) {
          group = c.name;
          groupMethod = undefined;
          prevKind = "group";
          touch(panel);
        } else {
          panel = cur = newSection(c.name);
          group = groupMethod = undefined;
          prevKind = "heading";
        }
        firstRow = false;
        continue;
      }
      // narrative: belongs to the last test, and ends an open panel
      panel = null;
      group = groupMethod = undefined;
      if (cur) {
        cur.notes = cur.notes ? `${cur.notes}\n${line.text}` : line.text;
        touch(cur);
      }
      prevKind = "other";
    }
    if (breaks.some((y) => y > prevY)) panel = null; // an interpretation image after the last row ends the panel too
  }

  out.sample.sampleIds = uniq(out.sample.sampleIds);
  const first = (xs: string[]) => xs.find(Boolean);
  out.dates = { collected: first(colls), registered: first(regs), reported: apprs.filter(Boolean).sort().pop() };
  return out;
}
```

## File: src/labs/common.ts

```ts
/** What a lab parser hands back before signatories and accreditation are resolved (see index.ts). */
import type { PdfImage } from "../pdf";
import type { ExtractedReport, LabId } from "../types";

export interface SignatureSighting {
  page: number;
  image?: PdfImage;
  /** printed name / title lines beside the signature (Clinova); Hy Patho prints none */
  nameLine?: string;
  titleLine?: string;
}

export interface LabParse extends Pick<ExtractedReport, "patient" | "sample" | "dates" | "tests" | "warnings"> {
  lab: LabId;
  labName: string;
  processedAt?: string;
  signatures: SignatureSighting[];
}

export const FOOTER_PAGE = /^(?:page\s*)?\d+\s*of\s*\d+$/i;

/**
 * Join a wrapped cell. Comma lists are wrapped mid-word ("Cotrimoxazol" + "e,Nitrofurantoin"), so glue
 * when the continuation starts lower-case and its first token runs into a comma or slash; else a space.
 */
export const joinWrapped = (a: string, b: string) => (/[A-Za-z]$/.test(a) && /^[a-z][^\s,/]*[,/]/.test(b) ? a + b : `${a} ${b}`);
```
